blockingFindings.issue: Original DB identity and owner are checked only on Service::open. Later commands reopen pathname using db::open READ_WRITE|CREATE without original entity/instance binding. If DB is moved/replaced during service lifetime, set_project can upsert projects in a replacement legacy/desktop DB before any ownership rejection. Missing DB is also silently created.
blockingFindings.requiredFix: Retain original DB handle/identity; check each new connection and transaction against it including SQLite HAS_MOVED, no CREATE on reopen, reject missing/replaced owner before writes. Add live move/replacement/missing-file zero-write fixtures.
blockingFindings.relatedEvidence: db.rs:12-18 flags CREATE; bootstrap:188-206 initial-only check; 243-263 later upsert; current foreign DB fixture only covers startup.

blockingFindings.issue: Oversized/non-scalar invalid id is echoed through failure(id,...). 64KiB limit covers only successful result Values. A valid-size <=128KiB input frame with e.g.100KiB id produces error response above output budget.
blockingFindings.requiredFix: Use null for invalid IDs and enforce serialized byte limit for complete success/error envelopes. Cover oversized scalar and structured IDs.
blockingFindings.relatedEvidence: response validation -> failure -> unconditional run_stdio serialization; static control flow, not executed.

blockingFindings.issue: Bootstrap validates raw target elements, but original draft_rows splits each URL again at comma/semicolon. One URL https://safe.invalid/a;https://user:pw@other.invalid/b has no outer userinfo yet becomes a credential-bearing second stored target. 32 raw elements can become up to original 200-target cap.
blockingFindings.requiredFix: Validate exact normalized target set and final32 cap, or reject original splitter delimiters in closed bootstrap input without changing desktop semantics. Add split-userinfo/count expansion fixtures.
blockingFindings.relatedEvidence: Unchanged original splitter/dedup/200 cap runs after new per-raw-element validation.
